# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 19 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_019_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 19

**19:1** They reached the entrance to the cave. A radiant cloud settled over it like a tent. The midwife whispered: "My soul is lifted up today — my own eyes have seen something extraordinary. Salvation has been born to Israel tonight." Then the cloud rolled back. A blaze of light poured out from inside the cave, so blinding they had to shield their eyes. Slowly, slowly the light faded, and there — in the dimness — was the baby. He found his mother Mary's breast and nursed.

**19:2** The midwife stood there stunned. "This is the greatest day of my life," she breathed. "I have seen something that has never been seen before."

**19:3** She came back out of the cave and found a woman named Salome waiting. "Salome!" she said. "Salome! You won't believe what I just witnessed. A virgin has given birth. I saw it. It shouldn't be possible, but it happened."

**19:4** Salome was skeptical. "I swear to God — unless I examine her myself, I won't believe a virgin gave birth. Not for a second."

**19:5** The midwife went back in and told Mary: "Hold on — things are about to get uncomfortable. Someone out there doesn't believe you." Salome came in and began her examination. The moment she did, she screamed: "What have I done? My own wickedness, my own unbelief — I have tested the living God, and now my hand is on fire — it's burning away!"

**19:6** Salome dropped to her knees. "God of my fathers, remember me! I am a daughter of Abraham, of Isaac, of Jacob. Please don't let me become a public example, a cautionary tale. Give me back to those who are poor and helpless — you know I have served in your name my whole life. You owe me nothing, but please — mercy."

**19:7** An angel of the Lord appeared before her. "Salome! Salome! God has heard your prayer. Go to the child. Touch him. Pick him up. You will find healing and joy."

**19:8** Salome stepped forward and lifted the baby into her arms. "I worship you," she said softly, "for you are a king born to Israel." Her hand healed instantly. She walked out of the cave a different woman — acquitted, overflowing with praise. Then a voice came from somewhere: "Salome — don't tell anyone what you have seen here. Not until the child comes to Jerusalem."
